The main takeaway from our work is that

the CF is an example of transpressive dextrally sheared shear zone, which developed in the Maures Massif during the late Carbonifero-Permian and is contemporaneous with the Corsica–Tanneron shear zone in Sardinia.
the Maures–Maures Tanneron Massif and Sardinia are two distinct tectonic units that separated during the Oligocene–Early Miocene due to the extension of the Western Mediterranean.

the CF is part of a regional-scale transpressive shear zone, the East Variscian Shear Zone (EVSZ) that was active during the Variscan orogeny, and that it was active after the Corsica– Sardinia Block and the Maures– Tanneron Massif were already separated.
